q: Quantum expanders are quantum channels (completely positive trace-preserving maps) that rapidly mix quantum states. Their spectral gap λ (second largest singular value of the channel's Kraus representation) determines the mixing time as:
opts: O(log(d) / (1−λ)) where d is the Hilbert space dimension — identical to classical expanders
exp: Quantum expander mixing: the trace-norm distance to the maximally mixed state decays as (1−λ)^t after t applications. Mixing time ≈ log(d)/(1−λ), identical in form to classical random-walk mixing. Quantum expanders are used in quantum error correction, quantum pseudorandom unitaries, and quantum complexity.
